evidence.observation: The lane surface is the intent -> effect -> settlement contract in one interface: `accept(request)` admits a durable intent and returns an `OperationAdmission`; `drive(options)` advances the admitted operation's in-flight effect; `getResult(operationId)` reads the settled `OperationResultRecord`. Because admission, driving, and result retrieval are separate awaitable steps, a settled operation survives process restart and can be inspected without re-running the effect.

The durable intent union: prompt (text or AgentMessage), skill, prompt_template, compaction, or navigation, each optionally carrying a caller-supplied `operationId`. Intent is fully classified before any model or tool effect is dispatched, which is what lets the harness persist and later resume the operation.

Admission receipt `{ operationId, kind, startedAt }` records the accepted intent and its family (run/compaction/navigation); the paired `OperationAdmissionError` union (LaneBusy, InvalidMessage, UnknownSkill, UnknownTemplate, NothingToCompact, InvalidNavigation, UnknownTarget, Closed) rejects the intent before any effect runs, keeping at most one in-flight operation per lane.

Effect progress is modeled as a three-way outcome: `settled` carries the terminal `OperationResultRecord`; `waiting` with `reason: "retry"` carries `notBefore`; `waiting` with `reason: "deferred"` carries a `DeferredHandle`. A failed-but-retryable effect therefore suspends as durable waiting state instead of collapsing the operation.

The `run_end` settlement event is discriminated by status: `completed | aborted` declare `error?: never`, while `failed` requires an `OperationError` (code/message/details). A failed effect is thus settled as observable data on the same event stream that announced `run_start`, and never as an untyped throw.

The run settlement result is `Result<OperationResultRecord | SuspendedRun, LaneBusy | InvalidMessage | UnknownSkill | UnknownTemplate | Closed>`: success yields the terminal record (or a deferred suspension), and the error channel is reserved for admission-time failures, cleanly separating intent rejection from failed-effect settlement.

`SuspendedRun { operationId, status: "suspended", deferred }` is the observation of an operation whose effect yielded a deferred handle; it is the non-settled branch of `RunResult`, showing that `deferred` is an effect suspension rather than a terminal outcome.

`AgentHarnessConstructor.create()` attaches the durable harness to one open session and returns `{ harness, open: OpenOperation[] }`. Returning the set of currently open operations on attach is what makes intent/effect state durable: a restarted harness rehydrates in-flight operations instead of losing them.

The persisted intent record: `operationId`, `lane`, `sourceTipId`, `startedAt`, and a discriminated `intent` of run (promptEntryIds), compaction (customInstructions), or navigation (targetId/summarize/label/instructions). This is the durable 'intent' leg of the pipeline, distinct from the terminal observation.

The immutable settlement record written by one terminal transaction: `operationId`, `kind`, `status` from `TerminalStatus = "completed" | "declined" | "aborted" | "failed"`, an optional `OperationError`, `fromTipId`/`tipId`, and `startedAt`/`endedAt`. A failed effect is represented by `status: "failed"` plus `error`, with no partial state left behind.

One of three `*.effect_pending` durable leaves (assistant, deferred, summary). It records that a non-idempotent model request has been dispatched (`attempt`, `responseEntryId`, `usageId`) and its outcome is not yet durably recorded, which is exactly the in-flight 'effect' phase between intent and settlement.

`AssistantRetryWaitOperation extends OperationScope, AssistantGenerationScope, RetryWait`; `RetryWait` carries `nextAttempt`, `notBefore`, and `errorMessage` (lines 203-207). This is the failed-effect recovery path: the failure is persisted as a durable wait leaf and the operation resumes on the next drive without replaying the completed effect.

The flat durable state machine with 13 family-neutral dispatcher leaves, including three effect_pending leaves, two retry_wait leaves, checkpoint/starting, tools, and navigation.ready_to_commit. Persisting this union (not just an in-memory enum) is what makes each intent->effect->settlement transition crash-recoverable.

Constructs the terminal settlement from the intent's `OperationMeta` and enforces the contract `(status === "failed") !== (error !== undefined)` by throwing `SessionInvariantError("Only a failed operation result may carry an error")`. Failed-effect handling is therefore exact: an error exists iff the operation settled as failed.

The `{ ok: true; value } | { ok: false; error }` union, plus `Result.ok`/`Result.err`/`isOk`/`isErr`, is the repository-wide envelope for both admission (`OperationAdmissionResult`) and settlement (`RunResult`). It is the typed channel that carries intent rejection or failed-effect errors without exceptions.

claims.claim: A pi operation is a durable, classified intent before it is anything else: `AgentLane.accept()` admits an `OperationRequest` (prompt/skill/prompt_template/compaction/navigation) and returns an `OperationAdmission` carrying operationId, kind, and startedAt, while `OperationAdmissionError` rejects the intent (e.g. LaneBusy) before any model or tool effect is dispatched.

The harness models an operation as three separate, resumable legs rather than one call: `accept()` records intent, `drive()` advances the in-flight effect and returns a `DriveOutcome` that is either `settled` or `waiting` on retry/deferred, and `getResult(operationId)` retrieves the settled `OperationResultRecord`; `AgentHarness.create()` even returns the currently open operations so a restarted harness rehydrates them.

A failed effect settles as typed data, never as an unhandled throw: the `run_end` event's `failed` variant requires an `OperationError` while `completed`/`aborted` declare `error?: never`, and the immutable `OperationResultRecord` mirrors that with `status: "failed"` plus an optional `error`. `RunResult`/`SuspendedRun` keep admission failures and effect settlement on distinct channels.

In-flight and failed effects are durable states, not transient memory: the assistant/deferred/summary `effect_pending` leaves record a dispatched non-idempotent request before its outcome is known, and the `assistant.retry_wait`/`summary.retry_wait` leaves (RetryWait: nextAttempt, notBefore, errorMessage) persist a failed-but-retryable effect so the operation resumes without replaying the effect. `OperationState` is the persisted 13-leaf union that carries these transitions across restarts.

Settlement is single, immutable, and invariant-checked: `operationResultRecord()` builds the terminal record from the intent's `OperationMeta` and throws `SessionInvariantError` unless `(status === "failed") === (error !== undefined)`, so a failed effect is represented exactly once and an error never attaches to a non-failed settlement.

All three legs are expressed through the repository's `Result` envelope: `OperationAdmissionResult` and `RunResult` use `{ ok: true; value } | { ok: false; error }`, so intent rejection (LaneBusy/InvalidMessage/...) and failed-effect settlement are both typed, inspectable outcomes rather than exceptions.

conclusion: In pi, an operation is modeled as a durable pipeline with three legs. Intent is an admitted, classified request (`OperationRequest` -> `OperationAdmission`/`OperationMeta`, kinds run/compaction/navigation) persisted as `OperationState` before any side effect. Effect is the in-flight phase: a non-idempotent model/tool/summary request is recorded as an `effect_pending` leaf, and a retryable failure becomes a durable `retry_wait` leaf (RetryWait) that resumes on the next drive instead of re-running the effect. Settlement is one immutable terminal transaction producing `OperationResultRecord` with `TerminalStatus = completed | declined | aborted | failed`; a failed effect settles as `status: "failed"` plus an `OperationError` (code/message/details) on both the record and the `run_end` event, and `operationResultRecord()` enforces that an error is present iff the status is failed. The executable demo in `.prale-eval/operation-pipeline.demo.ts` reproduces this model against the repository's real `Result`/`LaneBusy` types and normalized result shape, covering success, durable retry, terminal failure, and abort.
